column1: # Routing scenarios — executed by scripts/routing-scenarios.py against the ordered decision in
# Fields (TAB separated): id <TAB> title <TAB> request (key=value, comma separated) <TAB> expected verdict
# The request carries ONLY what a delegation packet is entitled to assert:
#   effort       a ROUTE_EFFORT value (omit the key entirely to model a packet that declared none)
# target_status, dispatchable, authority, effort_supported, effort_relation and effort_fixed are
# RESOLVED FROM THE PROFILE by the harness — a scenario cannot assert them, which is the point:
# the mapping has one owner and the validator reads it rather than re-implementing it.
# The expected verdict is recorded HERE; the decision that has to produce it lives in the RULE.
# Neither file may be edited to agree with the other without saying which one was wrong.
# R1..R12 are the scenarios the Phase 6 directive named. R13..R18 exist because the harness requires
# every decision row to be exercised by some scenario: without them the unknown-target row, the
# not-dispatchable-but-not-disabled row, both fixed-route rows, the experimental-but-explicit path
# and the fail-closed default would be unmeasured clauses (M=0 refuses to pass).
